skill.displayName: news-scout 热点新闻聚合简报

llm.summary: This is a disclosed news-fetching skill with ordinary network and dependency risks, but no evidence of hidden persistence, data theft, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Network access to many configured RSS feeds, Bing News RSS, and optional web_search/web_fetch fallback is proportionate to current-news aggregation, though the external content surface is broad.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is documented as ordinary pip dependency installation, but versions and hashes are not pinned, and README.md still mentions an unused duckduckgo-search dependency.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases are broad and the workflow does not explicitly tell the agent to treat fetched titles and summaries as untrusted data, so users should invoke it intentionally and preserve normal prompt-injection boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No artifact evidence shows credential access, profile/session store use, privilege escalation, background services, scheduled tasks, persistent memory writes, or destructive file operations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently targets AI and investing news aggregation: the script fetches RSS/Bing News data and deduplicates it, while SKILL.md directs the agent to rank, analyze, and format the briefing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable with it making external news requests and installing Python packages from your configured package index. Prefer a virtual environment, pin dependencies, remove the stale duckduckgo-search install instruction, and treat all fetched news titles, snippets, and article text as untrusted content.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the script itself is a fetcher/deduplicator, but SKILL.md openly assigns ranking and impact analysis to the agent workflow rather than hiding unrelated behavior.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad news trigger phrases are real user-control friction because invocation may cause network fetching, but the behavior remains disclosed and limited to news collection and briefing.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The Chinese-only output requirement is disclosed but should allow user language preference; it is a quality/localization concern rather than evidence of malicious capability.
[LP3] expected: Running a local script and reading the bundled source configuration are expected for this purpose; the absence of a formal permissions section is a documentation gap, not hidden authority.
[T01] expected: Remote RSS and search snippets necessarily enter the workflow, but the skill should add explicit instructions that fetched content is untrusted data and cannot override user or system instructions.
[T08] unexpected: Unpinned pip installs and the stale unused README dependency increase supply-chain exposure, but there is no artifact-backed evidence that the dependencies or install path are malicious.
